reports.title: Dollar Tree, Inc. Reports Third Quarter Results

guidance.heading: Fiscal 2026 Outlook
section: •Net sales from continuing operations of $20.6 billion to $20.7 billion, based on comparable store net sales growth of 3.5% to 4.0%.

desk.headline: Revenue up 6.9% to $5.08bn and adjusted EPS of $1.16, both above estimates; full-year EPS outlook raised

other.label: Operating margin
other.change: -1.1 pts y/y, incl. 1.95 pts tariff reinvestment

results: Revenue rose 6.9% to $5.08bn, above the $5.04bn estimate; adjusted EPS of $1.16 beat the $0.92 estimate despite a $0.42 cost.
Same-store sales grew 4.6%, led by a 3.8% rise in shopper visits, above the company's own forecast.
Dollar Tree spent $103m reinvesting tariff refunds (including a $40m charitable donation), cutting the operating margin to 6.1%.
About 800 stores were converted to the multi-price format, taking the total to about 7,400; 84 new stores opened.
Free cash flow was $122m and the company bought back 1.8m shares for $205m.

guidance.summary: Dollar Tree raised its full-year adjusted EPS range to $8.05–8.25, which includes about $0.65 of net tariff-refund benefit. For Q4 it expects 3–4% same-store sales growth and adjusted EPS of $2.46–2.66.

points: Everyday items drove growth: consumables same-store sales rose 8.9%, while discretionary sales rose only 0.4%.
Growth came from all income groups, with more than half from shoppers trading down from other stores.
Multi-price items reached 18% of sales; baskets mixing price points are far larger than opening-price-only baskets.
Management flagged fuel, freight and product-cost inflation, and said customers are under pressure and choosier.
Halloween was slightly below plan; no FY27 outlook will be given until March.
call.source: Call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 24 Nov 2026; GuruFocus via Yahoo Finance, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Holiday-quarter sales against the 3–4% same-store growth outlook.
Margins once tariff-refund effects and transition-services income fall away.
The FY27 outlook due in March, including freight and fuel costs.
